**Cause:** `leaks()` in `src/leaks.py:8` runs `json.dumps(actions)` before searching, and JSON escapes every backslash as `\\`. The transcript text becomes `C:\\Users\\dana`, but the secret `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, so the substring test at line 9 never matches. `/home/dana` has no backslashes, so it survives serialization unchanged, which is why the POSIX form is caught.

I reproduced it with `python3 -I`: the transcript containing `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt` returns `[]` for the secret `C:\Users\dana`, while `/home/dana` in a command is found.

The escaping is only one part of the problem. Because the check only looks at the JSON-encoded text, any secret containing a backslash, quote, or other character JSON escapes will fail the same way. The tests don't cover this: `tests/test_leaks.py` only uses forward-slash paths and a bare user name.

I didn't change anything in `src/`. The fix belongs to the other session. One direction for it: search the raw strings in each field (or search both the raw and JSON-escaped forms of each secret) rather than the serialized JSON.
